payload.feature:
BOUND THE TRANSCRIPT PROJECTOR, SECOND VISIT — issue #277. Branch slice-projector-bound at HEAD 043c9df3. Both blockers your predecessor raised are CLEARED; its specification work is adopted.

YOUR PREDECESSOR WAS RIGHT AND THE COMMISSION WAS WRONG. Run bound-the-transcript-projector-i-710eba02 parked at SPECIFY-UPSTREAM rather than proceed, and it was correct twice:

  1. **The scope fence was wrong.** The operator's merge ruling makes
     `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/transcript_command.rs::packed_dsh_members_have_separate_selectable_turns`
     wrong BY DESIGN — it asserts four separately selectable turns where the
     merge rule gives two — and two neighbouring suites depend on the same
     shape. The commission fenced those files out, so it asked for
     authorisation and refused both to bypass the suite and to keep a stale
     assertion. That refusal is the behaviour this house wants.
  2. **Cargo really was unavailable to its seats**, and it said so instead of
     claiming results. The worktree was fresh, so a read-only, network-free
     box had no warm target to build against.

**THE FENCE IS NOW WIDENED.** These three files are explicitly IN SCOPE, and correcting their assertions to the merged shape is part of the work, not a liberty:

    crates/brokkr-cli/tests/transcript_command.rs
    crates/brokkr-cli/tests/transcript_surfaces.rs
    crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui/tests.rs

Correct them to what the ruling requires and say, in each, why the number changed. A reader meeting `two turns` where the file used to say four must find the reason beside it.

**THE BUILD CACHE IS WARMED AND VERIFIED.** The controller built the workspace in this worktree and confirmed, by running `cargo test -p brokkr-view --all-features --locked` inside the same box specification your seats get, that cargo resolves and runs there. If a seat still cannot run cargo, that is a NEW fact worth reporting, not the old one.

ADOPT, DO NOT REDO. Three commits stand: `b82d2479` (specify), `555ad9f8` (design, with both council positions reconciled under Decisions), `043c9df3` (the dependent-test scope answer). Strict OpenSpec validation passed 15 items at that head. Do not re-plan what is settled; the design already names complete-prefix facts then bounded projection, packed coalescing, the shared 512-byte charge, the blockless guard, both lows, independent removal proofs and a named peak-RSS measurement method.

THE DEFECT AND THE RULING, restated so this commission stands alone.

`crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript.rs` allocates per event with no cap, so a bounded 32 MiB DSH session expands roughly an order of magnitude in memory on the operator's own console:

  (a) `dsh_packed` (:2669-2708) allocates one `DshEvent` per non-empty packed member — roughly 330 bytes for a member costing 6 source bytes. About 5.6M events, roughly 1.8 GiB peak per read.
  (b) (:2441-2469) a 21-byte `{"type":"tool/call"}` row with absent data yields a full block-bearing event, about 15x.
  (c) (:1996-2010) `events.append` retains a BLOCKLESS `DshEvent` for every `tool/result` or `user/message` row with absent data, about 10x of pure waste until it is dropped at :2101.

`display_cap` (:793-806) charges TEXT BYTES ONLY, so none of it truncates. Shape (a) can leave up to 4M single-character turns inside the `TranscriptRead` that the TUI deep-clones and structurally compares every 250 ms, and that `--json` serialises in full.

**OPERATOR RULING, 2026-09-17: do BOTH — merge, and charge a constant.**
  - **Merge** consecutive packed members belonging to the same turn into one chunk. A streaming session packs one member per token, so this bounds the flood at its source. It changes a spec-defined turn's shape, which is why the spec delta is part of this work and why the three test files above must move with it.
  - **Charge a constant**: `display_cap` charges each event a fixed structural cost as well as its text, so a flood of tiny events truncates exactly as a flood of bytes does. The design names 512 bytes; justify that against the measured ~330 bytes per event and make the budget's unit explicit in the spec.
  Neither alone stops a pathological input; the operator took both knowing it costs more review.

**Shape (c) is behaviour-neutral** and is not part of that ruling — guard it. A blockless event never suppresses (:2062-2065 requires a non-omitted block), never indexes as a chunk, never yields a turn, and its sequence is already pushed at :2000-2004. `collect_codex` guards this exact shape at :1147 and `dsh_packed` at :2693; one place was missed.

TWO LOWS, fold them in:
  - `codex_record_id_is_allocated_once_and_shared_by_its_blocks` pins pointer equality and strong count before and after the association pass but asserts nothing DURING it, so reverting the defect `5aee618` fixed would leave it green. Make it assert during the pass and prove that by reverting `5aee618`'s change, watching the test fail, and restoring.
  - `crates/brokkr-cli/src/ui.rs:554-568` admits a 65,537-byte newline-less header at end of file where the spec requires refusal above 65,536. One byte.

PROVE THE BOUND, DO NOT ASSERT IT. Every number in #277 came from code reading and arithmetic; none was measured. Build a synthetic DSH session of a stated size whose members are one per token — the ordinary streaming shape, not an attack — and record peak RSS or a defensible proxy before and after, naming the method. A test pinning the bound must fail when the bound is removed; prove each by removal and say so. Report your own before and after numbers, never an estimate.

DO NOT lower `DISPLAY_CAP` to make the symptom go away. The cap's meaning is what the console will hold; shrinking it would trade a real capability for a smaller number.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE. `adapters/`, `crates/brokkr-protocol/`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs`, and anything under `openspec/changes/2026-09-09-226-session-resumption/` — work over those is in flight elsewhere. Frozen contracts, policy, reference and fixtures are untouched.

STATE OF THE BRANCH. Cut from main at 5ef4a842; main has since moved to 9da5ff92 and this branch does not carry it, which is fine — the controller reconciles before delivery. The exact coverage gate demands literal equality on lines, branches and functions, so every line you add is a line it will demand covered. fmt, clippy across all targets and features, the crate suites, both bundle compiles and strict OpenSpec validation must all pass.

HOW TO MEASURE COVERAGE. Use a writable disk-backed TMPDIR OUTSIDE the repository; an in-repo TMPDIR breaks the ledger tests. Boundary tests skip inside the box, which cannot create a bwrap namespace on this host, so in-box equality is unattainable and is not your failure (#286). Report your in-box numbers; the host measurement is the controller's.

TWO HOUSE LESSONS FROM THIS WEEK. Stage any file you are about to execute beside its target and `rename` it into place; never write at the target path (#255). And never assert a refusal as `is_err()` alone — assert the REASON, because a call that failed for an unrelated cause satisfies `is_err()` while the check under test is never reached.

IF YOU RUN OUT OF ROOM. Return `oversized`, never `broken`. Shape (c) and the two lows are the cheap half; the merge and the constant are the substance. If a blocker is genuinely upstream again, say so as your predecessor did — that was the right call, not a failure.

KNOWN ENVIRONMENT DEFECTS — do not rediscover them. #282: the installed DSH core forwards GIT_CONFIG_COUNT but filters GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0, so prefix any git call, git init in tests included, with `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`. #281: a DeepSeek seat records no turns and no tokens; a harness defect.

PROVIDER INSTRUCTION. No Claude seat; the Fable allowance is spent. Codex (gpt-6-astra at xhigh) holds triage, clarify, the chief architect, analyze and the review chief. DeepSeek (the stable deepseek-v4-flash alias, never the expiring experimental one) holds implement, the task planner and every design and review position.

REVIEW POSITIONS state findings and evidence. They do not direct a verdict, do not tell a gate where to send the work, and do not claim another office's power.

CONSTRAINTS. Commit completed work unsigned. Never push, merge, or start another Brokkr run from a seat; the controller owns remote CI, publication, integration and closure.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

members.correctness:
Correctness/fit review of 043c9df3..1f395adf (both implementation commits), with the adopted specification/design and relevant history read. No source fixes or commits.

Findings:
1. MEDIUM — The required throughout-pass charged-storage proof is incomplete (crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript.rs:2374,2399,2745; crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript/tests.rs:4389). RETAINED_TURNS increments only after successful collector admission; the only candidate hooks surround a successful packed flush. There is no observation of ordinary candidate construction, fact-pass payload retention, retained text bytes or charged bytes. The tiny-call test checks a slot count and returned text, so it cannot detect excessive intermediate bytes with fewer than 7,812 large turns, or payloads retained outside the collector. The three-event direct blockless helper test likewise is not the specified thousands-of-rows in-pass witness. Adopted D8 explicitly requires these lifetimes and an oversized ordinary-text removal proof. Current output tests pass, but they do not establish the full bound claimed by the implementation evidence.
2. MEDIUM — The committed measurement/removal record is not fully reproducible (openspec/changes/2026-09-17-bound-transcript-projector/design.md:550-612). It gives maxima and prose mutation descriptions, but omits the individual three-run RSS/elapsed observations, all elapsed-time results, exact compiler version/build and invocation commands, reproducible fixture-generation commands, and concrete removal commands/patches. D8 explicitly requires these, particularly elapsed time to assess the second parse on the polling path. Generated inputs survive only under ignored target/measure. I confirmed case A's stated size/hash and independently measured the existing candidate release executable: 16 turns, 16 blocks, 262,144 text bytes, 270,336 accounting bytes; RSS 6,820/6,748/6,792 KiB, wall time 0.05/0.05/0.05 s. That supports the candidate result but does not independently reproduce the baseline comparison or repair the missing record.
3. LOW — Unused suppression indexes are always built (crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript.rs:2543-2546). UniqueSegments sorts and allocates two endpoints per observed span even with no eligible assembly, including every version-three session where no chunk can be admitted. This retains avoidable source-sized allocation and sorting work on each refresh and misses adopted D2's explicit no-consumer optimization.
4. LOW — Measurement configuration leaked into normal regression tests (crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript/tests.rs:450 and six other non-measurement sites). BROKKR_MEASURE_KIND changes the decoder for fixed DSH fixtures. Reproduced with env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 BROKKR_MEASURE_KIND=codex cargo test -p brokkr-view --all-features --locked dsh_admits_numeric_zero_and_projects_messages: failure at line 464, zero turns versus two. The selector belongs to the ignored measurement harness; ordinary semantic tests should remain deterministic.

Validation independently passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; workspace/all-targets/all-features clippy with -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked; both self and verify bundle compiles; strict OpenSpec 15/15; git diff --check. Frozen/excluded paths are unchanged and the tracked worktree remains clean. Existing coverage-summary evidence reads lines 30,422/30,593, branches 5,067/5,080, functions 2,918/2,928; coverage was inspected, not rerun, and host equality/remote CI remain pending. No security residual identified by this correctness seat.

INJECTION: the projector stays a pure function (no fs, process, shell, SQL, path construction, or logging added to production); untrusted member text is only concatenated before the existing display sanitizer runs, and JSON mode still preserves controls as data, so coalescing opens no new sink (unchanged transcript_privacy.rs control-sequence and hostile-path tests pass). Removal-proof claims in design D8 are backed by tests with independently computed expected limits; I did not mutate source (read-only seat). FAIL-CLOSED: validate_packed preserves every structural, range and recorded-token check of the old dsh_packed (exact_keys, positions, seq0/time0 bounds, dt length/type, member strings, per-member seq/time reconstruction); any violation sets refused and project_dsh returns unsupported-format with zero turns before the projection pass, so a required unknown or invalid packed row anywhere in the complete admitted prefix is never hidden by the display budget (complete_prefix_refusal_survives_the_display_cap passes; the fact pass never stops early). The new Suppression::None arm is equivalent, not fail-open: with no eligible citing assembly no coverage entry exists, so every old latest_ordinal query was already None. display_cost uses saturating_add and the collector checks cost > remaining before subtracting (equality fits), so no arithmetic wraps into admission; flush_run measures the whole run before allocating and discards an over-budget chunk whole. The five expect() sites in the projection pass (packed row, gap, time) are locally proven unreachable: both passes walk the identical immutable admitted.text through the same deterministic dsh_row/validate_packed, and a refusal short-circuits before the projection pass, so they abort rather than admit; CitationCoverage's expect is safe because dsh_citations rejects start > end. These are robustness notes, not findings.

The only path read added is BROKKR_MEASURE_FILE inside #[cfg(test)] #[ignore] measurement functions; the generate_fixtures.py helper writes only under MEASURE_OUT (default 'measure') and is not part of the build.
